saints.name: Thomas Becket
saints.legacy: Defender of Church rights and martyr
saints.summary: Thomas Becket was the Archbishop of Canterbury and a martyr who stood against King Henry II's attempts to exert control over the Church. His unwavering commitment to ecclesiastical rights led to his assassination in 1170, making him a symbol of the struggle for religious freedom. He was canonized by Pope Alexander III in 1173, just a few years after his death, and is remembered for his defense of the Church's authority.
